To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a G‐rich DNA sequence folds into a two quartet basket‐type quadruplex and that a single A‐to‐T modification induces the switch to a three‐quartel structure.
the adenine‐rich loop of a G‐rich sequence is critical for the formation of an antiparallel two quartet G‐quadruple DNA structure.
a G‐rich sequence folds into two‐ or three‐quartets, depending on the sequence and the presence of A residues in the loop.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and efficient synthetic routes to a range of novel compounds.
the development of new and efficient methods of synthesis of biologically relevant molecules, including nucleosides and nucleic acids.
the structural analysis of the G‐quadruple DNA formed by the G‐rich sequence of the RANK‐L promoter region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

adenine residues are not necessarily detrimental to the formation of G‐rich G‐quadruples, but rather that they can play a critical role in stabilizing and influencing the structure of G‐quartets, as shown in the case of the G‐rich DNA sequence from the regulatory region of RANKL gene.

A‐driven structural changes in a G‐rich DNA sequence are the result of an intricate balance between base pairing and hydrogen bond formation, which in turn is influenced by the relative positions and orientations of G‐straps.
the A5‐G12 base pair is the key to the formation of a two‐quartic DNA G‐quadruxplex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of adenine in the loop region is important to stabilize the two‐quartets and the absence of adenine in loop region is important for the formation of three‐quartets.

we show that the adenine residue at position 5 in the GGGAGGG sequence is critical in stabilizing a G‐rich sequence in a two‐quartic basket‐type GQ structure, which is different from the three‐quartic basket GQ structure formed in the absence of the adenine residue.

the adenine‐driven structural switch from a two‐ to three‐quartets G‐quadruples provides new insights into the structural complexity of G‐rich sequence and may facilitate the rational design of drugs targeting G‐quadruple DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sequence of the loop is not the only factor determining the structure of G‐quartet DNA, and the presence of A residues in the loop is also critical.

the presence of a single adenine residue in a G‐rich sequence can have a profound influence on the formation of the DNA structure and the relative orientation of G‐stranded quadruplexes, and that the presence or absence of a specific residue in a sequence can be used to direct the folding of GGG‐tracts into different topologies.
the sequence and structure of the G‐rich DNA can be modulated by the loop residues and that the structural changes can be induced by single‐nucleotide modifications.
